title: WHY SPIRITUAL GIFTS DON'T GUARANTEE SPIRITUAL MATURITY
paragraphs: WHY SPIRITUAL GIFTS DON'T GUARANTEE SPIRITUAL MATURITY
Some of the most dangerous words Jesus ever spoke were not directed at atheists.
They were directed at people who did ministry.
People who prophesied.
People who cast out demons.
People who moved in supernatural power.
People who believed they were serving God.
And yet Jesus looked at them and said:
“Then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness.’” (Matthew 7:23)
That passage should make every believer pause.
Because it reveals a truth that many Christians desperately need to understand:
Spiritual gifts are not the same thing as spiritual maturity.
Power is not proof of intimacy.
Activity is not evidence of transformation.
And giftedness can exist where character is deeply underdeveloped.
This truth is uncomfortable because many churches celebrate visible gifts while neglecting invisible growth.
We applaud what can be seen.
God examines what cannot.
The difference may determine the direction of an entire life.
The Difference Between a Gift and Fruit
The New Testament uses two entirely different concepts when discussing gifts and maturity.
Spiritual gifts are called χαρίσματα (charismata).
The word comes from χάρις (charis), meaning grace.
A charisma is a grace-given ability bestowed by God.
Paul explains this clearly:
“There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit.” (1 Corinthians 12:4)
Notice something important.
Gifts are given.
They are not earned.
A believer may receive a gift early in their Christian life.
Some receive extraordinary abilities shortly after conversion.
The gift itself is evidence of God's grace.
Not necessarily evidence of the believer's maturity.
Maturity is measured differently.
Scripture points repeatedly to καρπός (karpos), meaning fruit.
Paul writes:
Fruit grows.
Gifts are given.
Fruit develops.
Gifts can appear suddenly.
Fruit requires seasons.
Gifts reveal the Spirit's power.
Fruit reveals the Spirit's influence.
One can be received in a moment.
The other is cultivated through surrender, obedience, suffering, repentance, and daily transformation.
This distinction changes everything.
A person may operate in gifts while still struggling with pride.
A person may preach powerfully while remaining immature emotionally.
A person may possess remarkable ministry abilities while lacking humility, patience, and self-control.
The Corinthian Warning
Perhaps no church demonstrates this truth more vividly than the church at Corinth.
Corinth was overflowing with spiritual gifts.
Prophecy flourished.
Tongues flourished.
Knowledge flourished.
Miracles flourished.
Paul openly acknowledged this.
“You are not lacking in any gift...” (1 Corinthians 1:7)
Yet only a few chapters later he writes something shocking.
“I could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as people of the flesh, as infants in Christ.” (1 Corinthians 3:1)
The Greek phrase is νήπιοι ἐν Χριστῷ (nēpioi en Christō).
Spiritual infants.
Babies.
Immature believers.
Think about what Paul is saying.
A church can be highly gifted and deeply immature at the same time.
That statement alone dismantles many modern assumptions.
The Corinthians had gifts.
They lacked maturity.
They had manifestations.
They lacked character.
They had power.
They lacked love.
That is why Paul inserts the famous chapter on love directly into the discussion of spiritual gifts.
Love was not a random interruption.
It was the correction.
“If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am a noisy gong...” (1 Corinthians 13:1)
The issue was never the gifts.
The issue was the heart using them.
When Giftedness Becomes a Mask
One of the greatest spiritual dangers is using giftedness to hide immaturity.
People often discover that their gift receives affirmation.
People praise them.
Invite them.
Follow them.
Share their content.
Celebrate their influence.
Slowly something dangerous begins to happen.
The gift becomes their identity.
Instead of finding security in Christ, they find security in usefulness.
Instead of pursuing holiness, they pursue visibility.
Instead of seeking transformation, they seek platforms.
The tragedy is subtle.
The person may still appear successful.
But God sees what audiences cannot.
God sees private pride.
God sees hidden bitterness.
God sees unforgiveness.
God sees compromise.
God sees what applause conceals.
This is why character matters more than charisma.
Charisma can attract people.
Character sustains the work of God.
Why God Cares More About Who You Are Becoming
Throughout Scripture, God consistently emphasizes transformation over performance.
David was not chosen because he looked impressive.
God said:
“Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7)
The Hebrew word for heart is לֵבָב (levav).
It represents the inner person.
Thoughts.
Motives.
Desires.
Character.
The place God examines most carefully is often the place people notice least.
God is not primarily building performers.
He is forming disciples.
He is not merely creating servants.
He is creating sons and daughters who reflect the image of Christ.
Romans 8:29 declares that believers are being conformed to the image of Jesus.
Notice the goal.
Not giftedness.
Christlikeness.
Not visibility.
Transformation.
Not influence.
Resemblance to Christ.
The Maturity Test Most People Miss
Many believers evaluate themselves using the wrong questions.
Do I have gifts?
Am I effective?
Am I productive?
Am I influential?
Scripture asks different questions.
Am I becoming more loving?
More patient?
More humble?
More forgiving?
More gentle?
More self-controlled?
More like Jesus?
The most mature person in the room is not necessarily the most gifted.
It may be the believer who quietly forgives.
The believer who serves without recognition.
The believer who loves difficult people.
The believer who repents quickly.
The believer who remains faithful when nobody is watching.
Heaven celebrates many victories that never trend online.
The Hidden Purpose of Spiritual Gifts
Spiritual gifts were never designed to make us impressive.
They were designed to make us useful.
Paul says gifts are given “for the common good” (1 Corinthians 12:7).
The purpose is service.
Not self-exaltation.
Edification.
Not admiration.
Ministry.
Not celebrity.
Whenever gifts become tools for personal glory, they are being used contrary to their purpose.
The Holy Spirit does not distribute gifts to magnify people.
He distributes gifts to magnify Christ.
The More Excellent Way
After discussing gifts extensively, Paul introduces what he calls:
“a still more excellent way.” (1 Corinthians 12:31)
That way is love.
Love outlasts gifts.
Love survives platforms.
Love remains when recognition disappears.
Love reflects Jesus.
One day prophecy will cease.
Tongues will cease.
Knowledge will pass away.
But love remains.
Why?
Because love is not merely something God gives.
Love is who God is.
The believer who pursues maturity understands something profound:
The greatest evidence of the Holy Spirit is not what happens through you.
It is what happens within you.
Not merely what God empowers you to do.
But who God transforms you to become.
The Question Every Believer Must Ask
The real question is not:
“What gifts do I have?”
The deeper question is:
“What kind of person am I becoming?”
Because at the end of life, Jesus will not be impressed by gifts He Himself gave.
He will examine what we did with them.
Whether love governed them.
Whether humility shaped them.
Whether obedience directed them.
Whether Christ was exalted through them.
And whether our public ministry flowed from genuine private devotion.
A gifted believer may attract a crowd.
A mature believer reflects Christ.
One impresses people.
The other transforms them.
Perhaps that is why Scripture never commands us to pursue greatness.
It repeatedly calls us to pursue holiness.
And when holiness and giftedness walk together, the Kingdom of God advances with extraordinary power.
When they separate, giftedness becomes dangerous.
When they unite, Christ becomes visible.
Maybe that is the warning many believers need today.
Not every powerful voice is mature.
Not every platform proves intimacy with God.
Not every gift reveals spiritual depth.
But the fruit never lies.
The real miracle is not that God can use a person.
The real miracle is that God can transform one.
Be honest before God.
Your testimony may encourage someone silently fighting the same battle.
One day your gifts will be remembered by few, but the Christ formed within you will echo into eternity.
